t:
The Secretary may authorize the expenditure or transfer of any no year appropriation in this title, in addition 
to the amounts included in the budget programs of the several agencies, for the suppression or emergency prevention of wildland fires on or threatening lands under the jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior; for the emergency rehabilitation of burned-over lands under its jurisdiction; for emergency actions related to potential or actual earthquakes, floods, volcanoes, storms, or other unavoidable causes; for contingency planning subsequent to actual oil spills; for response and natural resource damage assessment activities related to actual oil spills; for the prevention, suppression, and control of actual or potential grasshopper and Mormon cricket outbreaks on lands under the jurisdiction of the Secretary, pursuant to the authority in section 1773(b) of Public Law 99–198 (99 Stat. 1658); for emergency reclamation projects under section 410 of Public Law 95–87; and shall transfer, from any no year funds available to the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement, such funds as may be necessary to permit assumption of regulatory authority in the event a primacy State is not carrying out the regulatory provisions of the Surface Mining Act: Provided, That appropriations made in this title for wildland fire operations shall be available for the payment of obligations incurred during the preceding fiscal year, and for reimbursement to other Federal agencies for destruction of vehicles, aircraft, or other equipment in connection with their use for wildland fire operations, such reimbursement to be credited to appropriations currently available at the time of receipt thereof: Provided further, That for wildland fire operations, no funds shall be made available under this authority until the Secretary determines that funds appropriated for “wildland fire operations” shall be exhausted within 30 days: Provided further, That all funds used pursuant to this section must be replenished by a supplemental appropriation which must be requested as promptly as possible: Provided further, That such replenishment funds shall be used to reimburse, on a pro rata basis, accounts from which emergency funds were transferred.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision that lets the Secretary transfer no-year funds for emergencies such as wildland fires and oil spills, with replenishment by supplemental appropriation. The tempting reading is that the reference to a "primacy State" or to reimbursing other Federal agencies signals coordination, but the State is only the subject of a federal takeover of regulatory authority and the reimbursements stay inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted, heard, given a comment opportunity, or granted a right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary may authorize the expenditure or transfer of any no year appropriation in this title

opus.w: This section only lets the Secretary move emergency funds around and sets conditions on that. The State is mentioned only as a trigger for federal takeover of regulation; nothing requires consulting the State or any other outsider. Reimbursing other federal agencies and asking Congress for supplemental appropriations happen entirely inside the federal government, so they are not participation.
opus.s: shall transfer, from any no year funds available to the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement, such funds as may be necessary to permit assumption of regulatory authority in the event a primacy State is not carrying out the regulatory provisions of the Surface Mining Act
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions a "primacy State" and "reimbursement to other Federal agencies," which look like outside involvement. Neither one involves an outsider in a federal decision. The State reference only describes when the Secretary takes over regulatory authority, with no consultation of the State. The reimbursements and the request for supplemental appropriations stay inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to transfer funds for various emergency and regulatory purposes. While it mentions a 'primacy State,' the interaction described is a unilateral federal assumption of authority due to the State's failure to comply, not a consultation or coordination process with the State or other outside parties before a decision is made. There are no requirements for public comment, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with states/tribes/local governments prior to the federal action.
qwen_chat.s: shall transfer, from any no year funds available to the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement, such funds as may be necessary to permit assumption of regulatory authority in the event a primacy State is not carrying out the regulatory provisions of the Surface Mining Act
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the phrase "permit assumption of regulatory authority in the event a primacy State is not carrying out the regulatory provisions" implies a process where the State participates in a decision. However, this is a conditional trigger for federal action based on non-compliance, not a requirement for consultation or coordination with the State before the decision is made. The text describes a unilateral federal response to a State's failure, not a collaborative decision-making process involving outside parties.
